text: Vietnam, China leaders hold talks, proposing continued elevattion of strategic trust

General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) Central Committee and President of Vietnam To Lam held talks with General Secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and President of China Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on November 17, proposing the two sides continue elevating strategic trust.

The talks took place on the occasion of the Vietnamese leader's attendance at the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Week and bilateral engagements in China, reported the Vietnam News Agency.

Commending China's thorough preparations for and wished it success in organising the APEC Economic Leaders' Week 2026, the top Vietnamese leader highlighted Vietnam's hope to build upon the outcomes of APEC Year 2026 and called on China to support Vietnam in successfully hosting APEC Year 2027.

General Secretary and President Xi warmly welcomed and appreciated his guest's second visit to China in 2026, noting that it demonstrates the high regard that the Vietnamese Party and State, and General Secretary and President Lam personally, give to China-Vietnam relations, as well as Vietnam's support for the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting hosted by China.

He affirmed China's support for Vietnam's successful hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in 2027 and proposed that the two countries leverage their respective roles as APEC hosts in 2026 and 2027 to contribute to regional peace, stability, and development.

The top Chinese leader underscored the significance of the Vietnamese leader's state visit to China in April 2026, describing it as an important milestone in advancing relations between the two Parties and countries in the new era.

Reaffirming the priority attached to the development of Vietnam-China ties, both leaders spoke highly of the positive and comprehensive progress in bilateral relations, highlighted by strengthened political trust and close high-level strategic exchanges.

They noted that agencies and authorities at all levels on both sides have earnestly implemented high-level commitments and agreements, while significant breakthroughs have been achieved in trade, investment, and strategic infrastructure connectivity.

To further consolidate the positive momentum in bilateral relations, General Secretary and President Lam called on the two countries to continue strengthening strategic trust and elevating economic and trade cooperation to a new level characterized by greater balance, sustainability, and integration.

He also urged both sides to prioritize strategic transport infrastructure connectivity, particularly the effective implementation of cross-border railway projects linking Vietnam and China, laying a solid foundation for deeper economic integration and industrial cooperation.
The top Vietnamese leader called for enhanced cooperation in strategic energy infrastructure, particularly power grid connectivity.

He also urged both sides to make substantive progress in human resource development and requested that China provide additional scholarships for Vietnamese students, especially in basic sciences and strategic technologies.
General Secretary and President Lam proposed strengthening coordination in multilateral frameworks while expanding exchanges and cooperation in defence, security, and diplomacy.
These efforts, he noted, would help deepen bilateral relations, make cooperation more practical, and further enhance political trust between the two countries.

General Secretary and President Xi agreed on the importance of maintaining high-level strategic exchanges, intensifying the sharing of theories and experiences in Party building and national governance, and making greater use of existing cooperation mechanisms, including the Steering Committee for Bilateral Cooperation and strategic dialogues on diplomacy, defence, and public security.

He emphasized the need to achieve more tangible results in practical cooperation, reaffirming China's support for stronger connectivity between Vietnam and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, as well as southwestern China.

He highlighted the importance of aligning development strategies and advancing integrated transport infrastructure, particularly in railways, expressways, waterways, and power connectivity, while encouraging investment and fostering a favourable business environment for enterprises from both countries.

The top Chinese leader welcomed increased imports of high-quality Vietnamese products and expressed support for reputable Chinese companies to contribute to Vietnam's industrialisation and modernisation.

He further affirmed China's readiness to assist Vietnam in enhancing its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities, particularly in manufacturing and agriculture, while expanding cooperation in the green economy and digital transformation.
General Secretary and President Xi also called for closer coordination in multilateral forums, particularly within the United Nations, ASEAN-China, and Lancang-Mekong cooperation frameworks.
On maritime issues, the two sides engaged in frank and constructive discussions and agreed to continue implementing high-level common understandings on managing and resolving differences.
They reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining peace, stability, and cooperation in the region in accordance with the United Nations Charter and international law.
